notes.text: Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (ankle injury) and has missed the last 17 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Chris Kreider is out (lower-body injury), reported after he played in their last game.
Mike Matheson returned in their last game after missing 6 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, up from 6% last season.
Brett Pesce is day to day (illness) and missed their last game. He is a top-four defenseman. Jonas Siegenthaler has taken his spot beside Luke Hughes.
Anthony Mantha is on long-term injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 3 games.
Johnathan Kovacevic is on injured reserve and missed their last game. Dougie Hamilton has taken his spot beside Declan Chisholm.

story.head: Bratt’s favorite opponent
paras: The Canadiens (12-3-4) beat Boston 5-2 on Thursday, and the Devils (14-6-0) beat Washington 5-2 the same night. Going in, the Canadiens are second in the Atlantic (tied for fifth in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (tied for fifth).
The Canadiens’ record (.737) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely because they’re 7-5 in one-goal games. The Devils’ record (.700) is about what their chances are worth.

The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd), take more penalties than they draw (30th) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (29th). The Devils, by contrast, draw more penalties than they take (1st). They also rarely throw hits (2nd lowest) and throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (3rd). Something has to give when the Habs’ shooting runs into the Devils’ defense. Beyond that, the Devils’ power play (8th) could do real damage against the Canadiens’ penalty kill (23rd), though their penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way.

Cole Caufield (12 G / 6 A / 18 P in 19 GP) is tied for the Canadiens’ scoring lead. Lane Hutson (3 G / 15 A / 18 P in 19 GP) shares it. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Montréal. Jesper Bratt (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 20 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games.

Jacob Fowler (9-1-2 / .926 SV% in 12 GS) has been outstanding for Montréal and will likely start. Connor Hellebuyck (6-0-0 / .916 SV% in 6 GS) has been outstanding for New Jersey and will likely start.

items.text: Connor Hellebuyck has won all six of his starts this season, already the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history.
The Canadiens are newly without Chris Kreider, and have been without Ivan Demidov and Samuel Montembeault for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.
The Devils are newly without Brett Pesce, Anthony Mantha and Johnathan Kovacevic.
Juraj Slafkovský has two goals on chances worth about 6.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
